From: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@carewavehealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-21T16:12:00Z
Subject: Data residency and subprocessor details (CareWave procurement)

Kimberly —

Thanks for taking this. We’re working through procurement and the security questionnaire attached; a few items that are blocking legal review:

- Can Redwood confirm the primary processing region for our account will be the EU (Frankfurt) and that production data will not be persisted outside the EU except for the narrow cases described below?
- We need a list of subprocessors that may touch tokens/audit logs and whether any of those subprocessors have US-hosted infra.
- We have a specific ask around transient caching: our policy requires that any transient cross-border cache must not persist beyond 72 hours and must be auditable. Can Redwood commit to a maximum TTL and provide the mechanism for cache flush + audit evidence?

I’ve attached the CareWave_DPA_Questionnaire.xlsx with the checklist. Could you confirm what we should expect in a DPA addendum and timeline for signatures? Procurement target is end-of-month.

Thanks —
Oliver
Oliver Shaw

Appreciate the clear asks and the questionnaire. Short answers up front: our hosted production tier can be scoped to an EU primary (Frankfurt) for your account, and we maintain a subprocessors roster that we’ll share. There are narrow operational cases where ephemeral processing may occur outside the primary region (e.g., cache population during short failovers or routing anomalies), but those are bounded and audit-logged.

I’m looping in Marissa (Legal) and Vivek (Infra) to put concrete DPA/addendum language and a technical note on TTL/flush semantics. Neha (Privacy) will propose the audit language you can attach to procurement documents.

I’m attaching our latest subprocessor roster for your review (redwood_subprocessor_roster_v3.pdf). We’ll follow up with a draft addendum this week. What is your procurement team’s hard cutoff for signature?

Oliver —

Thanks for the questionnaire. From a legal/DPA perspective:

- We can propose an Addendum A (Data Residency & Transient Processing) that explicitly names the primary processing region (EU - eu-central-1 / Frankfurt) and the narrow exceptions where transient processing may occur in other regions for availability/failover.
- Suggested contractual language for transient cross-border processing: maximum TTL for transient caches, automatic flush-on-failover, and requirement for retention of audit logs for 365 days.

Question for you: is a 72-hour maximum TTL acceptable as a hard requirement, or do you require a 24-hour limit for classification? If 72 is acceptable we can include a “transient window <= 72 hours” clause; if you need 24h we’ll mark it as a negotiating point with Ops.

I’ll draft the addendum and circulate a DocuSign envelope once we align. Kimberly — please confirm operational constraints (Vivek if we need longer TTL for cold cache rebuilds).

Regards,

Subject: Re: Data residency and subprocessor details (CareWave procurement)

Oliver/Team —

Technical context to inform the addendum:

- Primary region: your account will be pinned to eu-central-1 for model serving, KV caches, and persistent logs. All write operations from your production traffic will target EU endpoints by default.
- Transient processing cases: 1) short-lived cache population during cross-region routing where an upstream request briefly touches a node in another region during network pathing; 2) burst offload to a nearby region when eu capacity is exhausted and on-call policies allow conditional failover. These are controlled by routing rules and are *not* used for long-term storage.
- Cache semantics: application-facing KV cache entries for prompt prefixes and model KV cache are TTL-based. For your configuration we can set a maximum TTL of 72 hours; default operational TTL is typically 4 hours. We can also enable an immediate flush API that will invalidate all account-specific cache entries within ~30s of invocation.
- Replication & logs: we do NOT replicate persistent logs outside EU by default. Audit logs of cross-region events (routing/failover) are shipped to your EU audit bucket; we can surface those events with timestamps and the node-region id. We retain those audit logs for 365 days per the proposed addendum.

Operational ask: if you require a 24-hour hard limit for TTL we need to validate for two scenarios: (a) very high concurrency warm caches (some warm entries may be rebuilt frequently); (b) during sustained capacity failover where a short burst >24h might be required to maintain availability. If you can accept 72h as a compromise we can commit contractually and provide the flush API + audit evidence.

Ops playbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example-redwood-subprocessors (read-only link included above).

— Vivek

Subject: Re: Data residency and subprocessor details (CareWave procurement)

Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the roster. A few notes from our side:

- Procurement can accept a 72-hour maximum transient TTL provided it is contractually capped and there is an operational guarantee (flush API + audit records).
- We’ll want explicit DPA wording that: (1) names the EU region as the primary processing region; (2) defines "transient cross-border processing" and caps it at 72 hours; (3) requires audit evidence to be delivered within 3 business days upon request.
- Please send a DocuSign-ready addendum and we’ll route it through CareWave Legal. Our internal deadline remains EOM; if you can get the DocuSign sent by Friday 2026-10-27 that will keep us on target.

Oliver

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@carewavehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-27T22:04:00Z
Subject: DPA addendum draft and audit wording (for review)

Oliver/Team —

Attached is a draft of Addendum A for CareWave (DPA_Addendum_CareWave_Draft.pdf). Key clauses I recommend: 

1) Primary Processing Region: "Redwood will designate eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) as the primary region for processing and storage of CareWave production data."

2) Transient Cross-Border Processing: "Transient cross-border processing (including ephemeral cache population and short-lived routing events) is permitted only where necessary for availability; any such processing will be limited to a maximum of 72 hours per discrete event, after which cached artifacts must be flushed or invalidated. Redwood will provide an API and operational procedure to trigger account-scoped cache invalidation that completes within 60 seconds in normal operating conditions."

3) Audit Evidence & Delivery: "Redwood shall retain audit logs of any cross-border processing events and provide machine-readable evidence (timestamped event records with node-region identifiers) within three (3) business days of a written request. Audit logs will be retained for 365 days."

4) Subprocessor Disclosure: "Redwood shall maintain and provide upon request an up-to-date subprocessor roster identifying subprocessors with access to account telemetry, logs, or cache artifacts; Redwood will notify CareWave within 30 days of material changes to that roster."

If the language above lines up with CareWave’s security requirements, Marissa — please convert to a DocuSign envelope and loop in Legal. Oliver — I’m happy to join a call if you’d like an ops walkthrough before signature.

Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel (Redwood Inference)
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Attachment: DPA_Addendum_CareWave_Draft.pdf
